description: Expected API paths from a single-stage `vespasian scan` of the REST API target (LAB-3890 T2, gap A1). Consumed by test_scan_rest in test/run-live-tests.sh. Unlike rest-api (two-stage crawl+generate), this exercises the scan command's full pipeline end-to-end. /api/subscribe is served ONLY as a static HTML <form> action (never linked or fetched), so its presence proves the analyze.ExtractForms augmentation ran inside scan. Parameter names may vary ({userId} vs {id}); validate_path_coverage matches params positionally. INTENTIONAL DUPLICATE — EDIT BOTH FILES: this file and its sibling test/rest-api/expected-paths.json are deliberately kept in lockstep. They exist as two files only because two different tests read them (test_scan_rest reads this one, test_rest_api reads expected-paths.json) and JSON has no comment syntax; the paths, total_paths, and POST-form expectations (post_form_paths, post_form_body_fields_by_path) are identical on purpose. Any endpoint added to or removed from the test/rest-api server must be applied to BOTH files — updating only one silently diverges the scan-rest and rest-api expectations instead of failing loudly. They match today because pipeline.Augment (and its ExtractForms step) runs in both ScanCmd.Run and GenerateCmd.Run, so the single-stage scan path and the two-stage crawl+generate path recover the same set. Divergence is only justified once that stops being true — e.g. a discovery or probe stage is added to one command and not the other, or scan starts seeing endpoints the crawl capture cannot carry — and whoever makes them differ should replace this note in both files with the reason.
